title: Hidden in Plain Sight
description: Familiar objects speak in clues, then words and patterns start hiding their own answers.

questions.prompt: I have keys, felt-covered hammers and strings, but I open no doors. What am I?
questions.hint: Here, a key is something you press rather than turn.
questions.explanation: A piano's keys operate hammers that strike strings. The other instruments do not combine all three features.

questions.explanation: A shadow is the region where your body blocks direct sunlight. Unlike paint or a photograph, it changes with your position.

questions.prompt: You shout toward a distant cliff. I return the same words a moment later, though nobody on the cliff speaks. What am I?
questions.hint: The sound takes a journey before you hear it again.
questions.explanation: An echo is delayed reflected sound: your shout travels to the cliff and back.

questions.prompt: I am a five-letter English word for a small piece of rock. Remove my first letter and I can mean a musical sound; remove the new first letter and I become a number. Which word am I?
questions.hint: Apply the deletions in order, without rearranging anything.
questions.explanation: STONE becomes TONE, then ONE. The other choices do not make both required words.

questions.prompt: Take BANANA, remove exactly one letter and insert it elsewhere. All other letters keep their order. Which string CANNOT result from that single move?
questions.hint: If the unique first letter finishes last, it must be the letter that moved.
questions.explanation: Moving B to the end produces ANANAB, not AANNAB. BNAANA and BAANAN are possible by moving one A and one N respectively; no single move produces AANNAB.

questions.prompt: A four-digit code uses only 0, 1, 2 and 3. Its digits count, in order, how many zeros, ones, twos and threes occur in the entire code. Its second digit is 2. What is the code?
questions.hint: Every digit is both a symbol to count and a claim about the counts.
questions.explanation: 1210 contains one zero, two ones, one two and no threes, exactly matching its digits. Testing the allowed digit counts with the second digit fixed at 2 leaves only this code.
